title: 我用30年总结的舞蹈第1课｜你会少走很多弯路

method.teacher_system: The teacher begins by framing the lesson as a deep immersive experience, then guides learners through a playful, geometric warm-up using shapes and patterns on the floor, and concludes with breathing and cooldown exercises.
method.signature: Using geometric shapes (circles, squares, triangles) drawn on the floor to guide footwork and spatial warm-ups.

practices.what: Teacher explains the warm-up, focusing on activating joints and soft tissues to prepare the body for dance.
Teacher introduces tracing geometric shapes like circles, triangles, and squares while walking to warm up.
Teacher walks in continuous square patterns on the floor to maintain steady movement and warm up joints.
Teacher transitions to walking and tracing triangular patterns on the floor with different foot directions.
Teacher walks in smooth circular patterns to make the body movement more fluid and natural.
Teacher uses arms to draw circles in space, coordinating upper body with footwork.
Teacher asks learners to notice their increased heart rate and encourages pacing.
Teacher leads breathing exercises, inhaling through the nose and exhaling through the mouth to cool down.

adaptations.adjustment: Make the square bigger or smaller and adjust speed according to your home space and comfort.
Change directions or step size as needed for your space.

adaptations.difficulty: Following exact arm and foot choreography
adaptations.adjustment: You don't need to match my movements completely; adapt them to your own body and feel.

beliefs.belief: Early dance training is mostly about understanding body mechanics rather than just copying specific dance moves.
Warming up through playful games is far more effective and engaging than repetitive, mechanical exercise.

feelings.response: The teacher explains that frustration happens when foundational principles are skipped, and promises to cover those essential basics step by step.

moments.says: The teacher welcomes the learner to this first dance lesson, sharing key foundational insights from thirty years of dancing experience to help avoid mistakes early on.
The teacher introduces a warm-up game using geometric shapes to move freely around the room, inviting the learner to follow along.
The teacher encourages the learner to follow their own body's capability rather than matching every detail of the teacher's movement exactly.
The teacher leads a slow walk around the space, guiding deep breathing through the nose and mouth to bring the heart rate down.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable of exploring movement naturally through simple, playful principles.

struggles.theme: Finding the final part difficult to execute

clicked.theme: Geometric breakdown makes movement easy to understand
Warm-up with favorite music is enjoyable

requests.theme: Looking forward to part two and future tutorials
Want a dedicated session explaining rhythm and musicality

meant.theme: Brought back childhood dreams and a love for dancing
Made dance feel accessible rather than out of reach

method.limits: Only the first segment focusing on warm-up and basic movement exploration was analyzed from the full curriculum.
